*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Causality** — causation and the structure of causal relations — causal order, definite and indefinite, and its combinatorics, topology and geometry; sheaf- and process-theoretic accounts of causality; causal models, causal inference and interventionist accounts of what a causal relation is; and the metaphysics of causation — exclusion, mental causation, causal emergence and closure, reciprocal causation (ADR-035).

| [THEORY-058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) v2 | Mental disorders are maintained by self-reinforcing causal loops rather than expressing a latent common cause, which is how they can outlast their triggers | Three traditions that do not cite one another for it put self-sustaining loops where a latent cause would be. Borsboom ([LIT-547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-547.md)) makes disorder an alternative stable state of a strongly connected symptom network, kept up by hysteresis after its trigger has gone. Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)) make it a threat meaning protected by the behaviour it drives. Kendler ([LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md)) finds causal loops across levels, from genes to culture. It says nothing about what starts a disorder. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) v2 | In List and Menzies's account of causes as difference-makers, a higher-level property that makes a difference to an effect is its cause, and its realizer is not, exactly when in some nearest situation without that realizer the property is realized differently and the effect still occurs; which holds depends on each causal system's counterfactual structure, not on levels a priori | List & Menzies (2009), [LIT-722](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-722.md). Take causes to be difference-makers. Then Kim's exclusion principle fails, and a revised one holds or fails system by system. Given that a higher-level property makes a difference to an effect, its realizer is not a cause exactly when some nearest situation without the realizer has the property realized otherwise and the effect present; the record re-derived this. The claim that higher-level relations are typically insensitive to their realizers is an observation about scientific practice, and Pernu disputes the paper's main example. Which systems meet the condition is [QUESTION-213](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-213.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-138](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-138.md) | X is a cause of Y exactly when some intervention on X with respect to Y would change Y, where an intervention is an exogenous causal process that alone sets X (M1), affects Y only through X (M2), is not caused by anything that affects Y by another route (M3), and leaves Y's causes off the path through X unchanged (M4); so defined, causation is not reduced to non-causal facts but is not viciously circular, and needs no human agent | Woodward, "Causation and Manipulability" (SEP, 2001; revised 2023), [LIT-713](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-713.md). A cause is what changes the effect under a surgical, exogenous intervention, defined relative to the effect by M1–M4. The account separates total from direct causes by combining interventions, and treats natural experiments as interventions. Active as the standard the record uses for what a causal claim asserts. This statement says nothing about invariance, proportionality or levels. | Active |
| [THEORY-171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) v3 | When the causal constraints on events depend on context, deterministic assignments that are causal in each context can fail to glue into one causal assignment, so causal structure is itself a source of contextuality | From Gogioso & Pinzani's trilogy: The Topology of Causality, [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), read in [NOTE-612](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-612.md), with the definitions of The Combinatorics of Causality, [LIT-800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md) ([NOTE-635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-635.md)). Over a space of input histories with the lowerset topology, causal functions form a separated presheaf, and on the space Θ₃ it is not a sheaf: two causal assignments on disjoint opens give one event two outputs on their common extension. That example was checked here, and it settles the claim. The source's Theorem 2.34, that the presheaf is a sheaf exactly when no two contexts impose incompatible causal pasts on a common event, is reported as the source's. Its proof was not read, and it is QUESTION-143. It does not say any physical or quantum data display the effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-177.md) v2 | In a binary cyclic system, the Contextuality-by-Default measure of signalling is twice the sum, over contents, of the least direct influence of context that a canonical causal model of the data must place on each content, and each content's least influence is the total-variation distance between its two marginals | Wang, Sadrzadeh, Abramsky & Cervantes (2021), [LIT-851](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-851.md), Proposition 1. It joins CbD's maximal couplings ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md), Theorem 3.3) to Jones's 2019 correspondence between couplings and canonical models, which the paper quotes and the record derives independently. | [THEORY-222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md) v4 | With uniform interventions imposed separately at each level, a coarse-grained macro description of a known discrete mechanism can have more effective information than the micro description it supervenes on, so the level at which effective information is highest can be a macro level | Hoel, Albantakis & Tononi (2013), [LIT-1038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1038.md), read in [NOTE-726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-726.md). Effective information is effectiveness (determinism minus degeneracy) times the log of the state-space size, measured under uniform interventions. Coarse-graining always loses size and can gain effectiveness; when the gain wins, causal emergence CE = EI(macro) − EI(micro) is positive. Four toy systems give 0.40 to 2.92 bits. The arithmetic is exact. The reading that the EI peak marks where causation happens rests on imposing a uniform distribution at each level, which the paper adopts and does not test; the title does not claim it. Promoted on 2026-10-20 on a construction. Whether the gain survives one intervention distribution at both levels is QUESTION-204. | Active |
| [THEORY-231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-231.md) v3 | Within classical realism, a generalized-noncontextuality no-go refutes Leibnizian representations, not realist representations as such; it rests on a stronger assumption than a Bell-like no-go and so applies where none exists, as in prepare-measure scenarios, but only Leibnizianity implying noncontextuality is proved | Schmid, Selby and Spekkens (2020), [LIT-945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-945.md), §VI.C, §VIII (Eqs. 200, 214, 215), read in part in [NOTE-737](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-737.md), which is Skimmed: §§II–IV and the proofs in Appendices C–G were not read. | [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md) v5 | In two optically trapped beads with a symmetric hydrodynamic coupling, one trap moved by a recorded noise drive, time-delayed mutual information and transfer entropy follow the drive's path rather than the coupling's symmetry: the flow between the beads reads two-way under moderate drive, in experiment and numerics, and one-way under strong drive, in numerics of the fitted model only | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee (2025), [LIT-947](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-947.md), read in [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md). | [THEORY-451](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-451.md) | A singular causal claim, that C will contribute or did contribute to E in a particular setting, is warranted only by joint evidence on each step of the causal process there, its causal principle, its support factors and the absence of its derailers, which no single method supplies; a well-run RCT secures at most the study population's average effect, and often not even that rigorously, and its result is not by its method evidence about any other population | Cartwright (2021), [LIT-213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-213.md), read in [NOTE-161](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-161.md). | [THEORY-485](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-485.md) | Wave-function realism falsifies causal closure restricted to spacetime but is compatible with closure relative to fundamental physics, so quantum ontology opens no causal gap for non-physical causes; what it forces on the physicalist is a criterion of the physical and a bridge from dynamical to causal completeness | Poltorak (2026), [LIT-164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-164.md), an unrefereed preprint read in full in [NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md). "Every physical effect has a sufficient physical cause" has two tacit parameters, a domain and a completeness relation. With the domain set to spacetime the principle fails under wave-function realism; with it set to the ontology of a complete fundamental theory it survives. The move to a breach needs a premise that wave-function realists deny. The conclusions are modest and close to analytic once the terms are defined. The target is conceded to be a picture, not a published argument, and the dynamical-to-causal bridge is asserted, not argued. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-491](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-491.md) | Of the five standard arguments that randomisation gives a clinical trial special evidential weight, only the selection-bias argument is sound, and it supports only taking allocation out of the experimenters' hands; given balance on plausible confounders, a placebo or active control and blinding, randomisation is argued to add nothing, since balance on unknown confounders is not even probable in the one division a trial makes | Worrall (2007), [LIT-175](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-175.md), read in [NOTE-126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-126.md). The case against the unknown-confounders argument is conceptual: frequentist balance is a long-run claim about repeated divisions, and a trial divides once. The conclusion is relative to the authors' definition of flow; transfer entropy as predictive improvement is untouched. The claims about directed information, interventional flow and Gaussian systems are cited or conjectured. | Active |
| [THEORY-710](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-710.md) | In a finite causal Bayesian network, a set of nodes is causally independent of another, imposing a third, for every choice of mechanisms exactly when every directed path between them passes through the third; information flow, conditional mutual information computed from interventional instead of observational distributions, vanishes under causal independence, and it can differ from transfer entropy and conditional mutual information in either direction | Ay & Polani (2008), [LIT-1174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1174.md), read in full in [NOTE-946](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-946.md) from the 2006 preprint. Theorem 2 and Prop. 3 are proved; Examples 3–6 were recomputed. Example 6's one bit holds at k = 1 and fails for k ≥ 2 as stated. The measure needs the mechanisms, and estimation and identification are not addressed. | Active |
| [THEORY-711](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-711.md) | Directed information from an input sequence to an output sequence, the sum over time of the information the inputs up to now carry about the current output given the past outputs, is at most their mutual information and equal to it when the channel is used without feedback; in a causal system it bounds what the output reveals about the source, so feedback cannot raise a memoryless channel's capacity; and the usual definition of a memoryless channel holds only without feedback | Massey (1990), [LIT-1166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1166.md), read in full in [NOTE-939](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-939.md) from the author's preprint. Three short theorems, all checked; the feedback inequality also checked numerically. "Causal" is Massey's factorization condition, not intervention. That directed information is full-history transfer entropy plus instantaneous terms is the record's derivation. | Active |
| [THEORY-764](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-764.md) | For a deterministic supervenient feature V of a Markov system, Rosas et al.'s practical emergence criterion Ψ equals the parts' whole-minus-sum information about V's next value minus V's one-step dynamical dependence I(V_t′; X_t \| V_t), so dynamical independence raises Ψ but neither implies emergence nor is implied by it, and the paper's sufficient test for causal decoupling can pass a feature that is not dynamically independent | Rosas et al. (2020), [LIT-1244](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1244.md), read in [NOTE-987](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-987.md), with Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence ([LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), [THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md)). By the chain rule, Ψ(V) = [I(X_t;V_t′) − Σ_j I(Xʲ_t;V_t′)] − I(V_t′;X_t\|V_t). The subtracted term vanishing implies Barnett–Seth independence for Markov X. Examples show each condition without the other. The independent sum of AR(1) channels has both, with no interaction. The identity concerns Ψ, the paper's practical criterion; it says nothing about the PID quantities themselves. | Active |
| [THEORY-787](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-787.md) | A system's causal structure can be most effective at a macro scale, so that causation emerges at a coarse-grained level and the macro description is the one at which the system's causes are found, as Hoel, Albantakis and Tononi propose from effective information | Hoel, Albantakis and Tononi (2013), [LIT-1038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1038.md), argue that macro can beat micro: the scale at which effective information peaks is where a system's causal structure is, so causation can emerge at a macro level. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md), only the arithmetic: under uniform interventions imposed separately at each level, a macro description can have more effective information. This is the causal thesis, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-801](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-801.md) | Agents are the systems that would adapt their policy were their actions to affect the world differently, so the agent is wherever that adaptation is: a thermostat is not an agent while it together with its design process is, an RL training process is while its learnt policy generally is not, and humans are | The definition and verdicts [THEORY-527](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-527.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 055) narrowed it to the recovery theorem. Kenton, Kumar, Farquhar, Richens, MacDermott and Everitt (2022), [LIT-909](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-909.md), propose the definition and argue the verdicts from it in §1 and §4; that it "reliably classifies humans as agents" is asserted. The verdicts are relative to the variables chosen, which the paper states. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-802](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-802.md) v2 | In trained networks as in constructed ones, interchange interventions on a fixed set of variables can be satisfied equally by alignments related by a change of basis, so which internal direction mediates a high-level variable is fixed only relative to a chosen decomposition into units, and complex models will generally have several distinct, fully correct abstractions | The general reading that [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the three-unit network it proves (batch 062). Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), conjecture that complex models have "multiple distinct fully correct abstractions" and that the causal-abstraction framework cannot settle structural equivalence; Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), §8, grant that crossing component boundaries makes "illusory" tenuous, and answer by privileging components. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. Its only support is the constructed tie. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-820](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md) v2 | For a stationary discrete-valued process X and any coarse-graining Z of its past, informational closure at every horizon is the same condition as zero one-step transfer entropy from the micro past, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, and as causal closure, Z's ε-machine coinciding with its υ-machine; for a coarse-graining of the present state it also makes Z's causal states a coarse-graining of X's, which does not imply closure, and the closed coarse-grainings are not closed under common refinement | Rosas et al. (arXiv 2024), [LIT-1306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1306.md), read in [NOTE-1030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1030.md), with Barnett and Seth's definition ([LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md)). For discrete stationary processes, the information-theoretic criterion of emergent closure (dynamical independence), the interventionist one (the macro's own causal states are all the micro distinctions that matter for it) and, for maps of the present state, a computational one are nested as stated. The first two are one condition. It says nothing about approximate closure. It does not make closure a mark of unity. "Causal" is only in the Granger sense unless X is fully observed. | Active |
| [THEORY-824](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-824.md) | Economics working papers increasingly back their claims with design-based identification: in NBER and CEPR working papers the share of claims supported by difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, an RCT, regression discontinuity or synthetic control rose about fourfold from 1990 to 2020 | Garg and Fetzer (2024; arXiv v2 2026), [LIT-079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-079.md), read in full in [NOTE-083](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-083.md), read the rise in their extraction's design-backed share as a change in economics: "economic papers have increasingly incorporated causal inference methods to substantiate their claims over the past three decades". The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-674](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-674.md), only the extraction's series, whose edges were never checked against human labels and whose per-decade slope nearly vanishes with method-mix and graph-volume controls. This is the paper's reading, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-839](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-839.md) | A model optimal for the distribution its own deployment induces, a performatively stable point, need not minimize the risk it actually incurs, and the gap is bounded: for a loss that is L_z-Lipschitz in the data and γ-strongly convex in the parameters, and a distribution map that is ε-Lipschitz in Wasserstein-1 distance, every stable point lies within 2L_zε/γ of every performative optimum; in a biased-coin example the stable point is µ/(1 − ε) and the optimum µ/(1 − 2ε), equal only when the prediction has no effect | Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner and Hardt (2020), [LIT-1336](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1336.md), read in [NOTE-1044](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1044.md). Self-consistency under one's own influence and the best outcome under that influence are different targets. The bound says they are close when the influence is weak relative to the loss's curvature. It does not say how to find the optimum, which needs the distribution map away from the deployed model. | Active |
| [THEORY-843](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-843.md) | Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern's approximate abstraction error, the least over surjective context maps of the worst case over allowed interventions and contexts of the high-level distance between the coarse-grained low-level outcome and the high-level outcome, is zero exactly for τ-abstraction; an abstraction followed by an α-approximation of the high-level model is within α, an α-approximation of the low-level model followed by an abstraction only within kα, k the worst-case ratio of high- to low-level distances, and an approximate abstraction need not factor into an exact abstraction and an approximation | Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern (2020; arXiv 2019), [LIT-1310](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1310.md), read in [NOTE-1045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1045.md), on Beckers and Halpern's τ-abstraction ([LIT-1316](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1316.md)). The error is relative to a metric the user chooses, takes the worst case over interventions, and minimizes over context maps, so like exact abstraction it is zero for a coarse-graining whose dropped detail the high-level noise can hold. It does not measure the governance deficiency Γ. | Active |
| [THEORY-847](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-847.md) | In a linear structural equation model whose exogenous micro-causes W₁, …, W_n drive effects Z = AW + F, with interventions that set all of W, all of Z or both, averaging each block is an exact transformation onto Ẑ = (an/m)Ŵ + F̂ if and only if every column of A sums to the same a, the column-equitability of the block of A from W to Z; the transformation is exact only for those whole-block interventions | Rubenstein et al. (2017), [LIT-1334](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1334.md), read in [NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md), with Beckers and Halpern's restatement ([LIT-1316](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1316.md), Example 3.3). Averages of linear micro-variables form a causally consistent macro model exactly when each micro-cause has the same total effect on the effect block. It says nothing about interventions on single micro-variables, which break exactness, nor about nonlinear or approximate aggregation. | Active |
| [THEORY-848](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-848.md) | In an acyclic structural equation model, marginalising a variable that no declared intervention sets is an exact transformation, provided the coarse model's exogenous noises may be dependent; so exactness does not require the dropped variable to be causally idle, and it can drop a variable that decides how its children respond to an intervention that is declared | Rubenstein et al. (2017), [LIT-1334](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1334.md), read in [NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md). Exact transformation asks only that the coarse model reproduce the push-forward of each declared interventional law, so a never-intervened variable can be substituted out and its randomness folded into noise, whatever it does. Applied to the hidden governance bit, the coarse-graining that [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md) shows to lose the response to h is exact. It does not say that the coarse model keeps any one system's response. | Active |
| [THEORY-849](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-849.md) | For deterministic causal models with a countable set of allowed interventions, a high-level model reproduces the coarse-grained interventional law of a low-level one for every distribution on contexts exactly when some map τ_U on contexts commutes with every allowed intervention, τ(M_L(u, i)) = M_H(τ_U(u), ω(i)); exactness for one distribution is strictly weaker, since a well-chosen distribution lets unrelated models match, and τ-abstraction and strong abstraction are strictly stronger; the context map is only required to exist, so high-level exogenous variables may carry what the coarse state drops | Beckers and Halpern (2019), [LIT-1316](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1316.md), read in [NOTE-1032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1032.md), on Rubenstein et al.'s exact transformation ([LIT-1334](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1334.md)). Uniformity over distributions turns a distributional match into a context-by-context commuting condition. It does not make the coarse endogenous state carry the high-level context, which is what governance-response sufficiency would need. | Active |
| [THEORY-861](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-861.md) | When a deployed model changes the distribution it is scored on, retraining on the distribution the last model induced contracts at rate εβ/γ, for a β-jointly smooth, γ-strongly convex loss and a distribution map that is ε-Lipschitz in Wasserstein-1 distance, and so converges to a unique performatively stable point when ε < γ/β; each condition is needed, since dropping strong convexity, joint smoothness or the bound on ε each admits a case where retraining never converges | Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner and Hardt (2020), [LIT-1336](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1336.md), read in [NOTE-1044](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1044.md). Retraining under performativity is a fixed-point iteration, and these are the conditions for it to settle. Its fixed point is self-consistent, not optimal ([THEORY-839](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-839.md)), and outside the conditions there may be several or none. | Active |
| [THEORY-889](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-889.md) | Among white Southerners today, those living in counties where a larger share of the 1860 population was enslaved are somewhat less Democratic, less supportive of affirmative action, more racially resentful and colder toward black Americans, by about a tenth of a standard deviation per standard deviation of slave share; the difference is not accounted for by the present black share of the population, and in voting it appeared after Reconstruction rather than before the war, which supports its origin in the incentives that emancipation gave planters to repress black labor and votes, and its local transmission thereafter | Acharya, Blackwell and Sen (2016), [LIT-1388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1388.md), read in full in [NOTE-1089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1089.md) from the journal PDF on the second author's site, without the online appendix. The association is well supported; the causal reading rests on 1860 controls, a cotton-suitability instrument with an untestable exclusion restriction, and a direct-effect estimate. The transmission mechanism has the weakest evidence: a parent–child correlation in 241 Southern respondents not linked to county slavery. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-965](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-965.md) | Sparse-autoencoder features of a large language model's residual stream are units the model computes with: they track abstract concepts across languages, modalities and concrete or abstract instances, and intervening on one changes the model's behaviour in the way its label predicts, better than directions found from a few labelled examples | Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md), with Bricken et al. (2023), [LIT-1545](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1545.md), for the one-layer case. The thesis of both papers: features are the model's own units, shown by steering. The authors' own hedges: steering needs features clamped beyond their observed range; the reconstruction error rides along; "we haven't rigorously evaluated our features against other steering methods". The record holds a result against it for known causal variables ([THEORY-968](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-968.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-966](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-966.md) | Greedy edge pruning of the ACDC kind, which removes each edge whose removal changes the output metric by less than a threshold given the edges already removed, keeps only one input of a redundant OR gate, and which input it keeps depends on the order in which edges are visited, so when a model has redundant sufficient paths the circuit it returns is one of several sufficient subgraphs | Conmy et al. (2023), [LIT-1547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1547.md), Appendix M, read in [NOTE-1170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1170.md). For out = 1 − ReLU(1 − x − y) with x = y = 1, removing either input alone leaves the output at 1, so the first one visited is pruned and the second is then kept; visiting y first keeps x instead. It does not say how common redundant paths are in trained models, nor that any other method does better: HISP keeps neither input. | Active |
| [THEORY-968](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-968.md) | In the Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark's causal-variable localization baselines on Gemma-2 2B and Llama-3.1 8B, features of the public Gemma Scope and Llama Scope sparse autoencoders, selected by a learned binary mask, never gave a higher mean interchange-intervention accuracy than the same mask over the model's own hidden dimensions, in all sixteen task–variable cells and by 1 to 14 points, while distributed alignment search, trained against the causal model it is scored on, gave the highest mean in fifteen of them | Mueller et al. (2025), [LIT-1550](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1550.md), read in [NOTE-1169](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1169.md). Unsupervised SAE features were worse units than neurons for known task variables across ARC, MCQA, two-digit addition and RAVEL. It does not say SAE features are never causal units: the comparison is on residual streams, under one selection method, with the base reconstruction error carried into every intervention, and the best method is supervised by the hypothesis it is scored against. | Active |
| [THEORY-970](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-970.md) | On three language-model tasks whose circuits earlier manual work reported, indirect object identification and Greater-Than in GPT-2 Small and Python docstrings in a four-layer attention-only model, ACDC run with resampled corrupted activations against KL divergence ranked the reported edges with areas under the ROC curve of 0.85 to 0.98, above head-importance pruning and subnetwork probing on all three; on two compiled tracr programs it ranked them poorly with corrupted activations, 0.68 and 0.20, and exactly with zero activations | Conmy et al. (2023), [LIT-1547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1547.md), read in [NOTE-1170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1170.md). Edge AUCs with corrupted activations and KL: Docstring 0.982, Greater-Than 0.853, IOI 0.869 for ACDC, against 0.805, 0.693, 0.789 for HISP and 0.937, 0.806, 0.823 for SP. It does not say ACDC finds the true circuit: the reported circuits are incomplete, the results depend on metric, ablation and parent order, and negative components are missed at sparse thresholds. | Active |
| [THEORY-974](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-974.md) | When a transformer's MLP sublayers are replaced by transcoders and the attention patterns and LayerNorm scales on a prompt are held fixed, the contribution of an earlier transcoder feature at the same token to a later one's pre-activation is the earlier feature's activation times the dot product of its decoder with the later feature's encoder, scaled by one LayerNorm constant per token, so the weight factor is fixed by the trained weights and holds on every input | Dunefsky, Chlenski and Nanda (2024), [LIT-1554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1554.md), read in [NOTE-1174](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1174.md), Eq. 7 and App. D.2–D.4, re-derived here. The weight factor is a weight of the replacement model, not of the original, and it is exact only for the replacement. It says nothing about why attention attends where it does, and "input-invariant" holds only up to a per-token LayerNorm scalar and only while the later feature is active. | Active |
| [THEORY-978](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-978.md) v2 | Causal scrubbing scores a hypothesis through the partitions of the dataset that its interpretation nodes induce, so two hypotheses that assign different features to a node but induce the same partition on the dataset, such as two features perfectly correlated on it, receive the same score | Chan et al. (2022), [LIT-1549](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1549.md), read in [NOTE-1168](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1168.md). In the causal-scrubbing algorithm an interpretation node enters only through sample_agreeing_x, which draws a datum with an equal value of that node, so only the equivalence classes the node induces on the dataset matter. The authors say it themselves: the method "doesn't allow us to distinguish between two features that are perfectly correlated on our dataset". It does not say that a passing hypothesis is otherwise wrong, nor anything about features correlated only imperfectly. | Active |
| [THEORY-979](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-979.md) | On one prompt, a transformer whose MLPs are replaced by a cross-layer transcoder, with its attention patterns and normalization denominators frozen and each MLP's reconstruction error added back as a constant, reproduces the model's activations and outputs exactly and is linear between features, so each active feature's pre-activation is the sum of its attribution-graph edges and constants; a perturbation that clamps MLP outputs up to the target feature's encoder layer then confirms a direct edge by construction, and tests only knock-on effects and the output | Ameisen et al. (2025), [LIT-1552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1552.md), read in [NOTE-1185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1185.md): the local replacement model, the edge formula and the appendix on steering, re-derived here. It is a statement about what an attribution graph is exact for, not about the model: exactness holds at the unperturbed point only, the error terms are constants with no inputs, and the frozen attention patterns are the part of the computation the graph does not explain. | Active |
| [THEORY-980](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-980.md) | In GPT-2 small on fifteen templates of indirect object identification, a circuit of 26 attention heads in seven classes, found by path patching, keeps 87% of the model's mean logit difference when every other head is mean-ablated; knocking out its three main name mover heads costs only 5%, because other heads take over, and knockout sets found by greedy search make the circuit and the full model differ by up to 87% of the logit difference, so the circuit is faithful on average and incomplete under knockouts | Wang et al. (2022), [LIT-1540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1540.md), read in [NOTE-1167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1167.md): §§3–4 and the appendices. The circuit implements "identify the names, remove the duplicated one, output the rest" through duplicate-token, induction and previous-token heads, S-inhibition heads and name movers, with negative and backup name movers. The faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests are the paper's own. It says nothing beyond these templates and this model, it treats MLPs as given, and its greedy search is printed in a form that does not match its description. | Active |
| [THEORY-983](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-983.md) | In Geiger et al.'s three-layer feed-forward network trained on hierarchical equality and in BERT fine-tuned on monotonicity inference, interchange interventions on subspaces found by a learned rotation aligned the hypothesised two-variable causal models with interchange intervention accuracy of 1.00 on the rotation's training data, where the axis-aligned alignment closest to the learned rotation reached 0.73 and 0.51; in BERT, the learned lexical-entailment subspace was in turn aligned, at 0.97 to 0.98, with a model holding only the identities of the two words | Geiger, Wu, Potts, Icard & Goodman (2024), [LIT-1551](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1551.md), read in [NOTE-1192](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1192.md). Layer 1 of the equality network (1.00 with \|N\| = 16 and two 8-dimensional subspaces) and layer 9 of BERT's [CLS] vector (1.00 with two 256-dimensional subspaces). It does not say the networks implement the algorithms in any stronger sense than interchange accuracy on training pairs, nor that the learned subspaces are unique: every rotation within them gives the same interventions. | Active |
| [THEORY-987](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-987.md) | In Claude 3 Sonnet's middle-layer residual stream, on two prompts for which every active sparse-autoencoder feature was ablated, how strongly a feature was active predicted its ablation effect on the answer poorly (correlation about 0.12) while its gradient attribution predicted it well (about 0.81), and on the multi-step prompt only three of the ten most active features were among the ten with the largest ablation effect | Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md): Features as Computational Intermediates and the appendix on ablations and attributions. On "The capital of the state where Kobe Bryant played basketball is" (Sacramento against Albany), the five features with the largest ablation effect, Kobe Bryant, California, capital, Los Angeles and the Lakers, rank as low as 70th to 162nd by activation. It does not say how often this holds beyond the two prompts, and for other prompts the authors found no intermediate features at this layer. | Active |
| [THEORY-994](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-994.md) | In Ameisen et al.'s evaluations, the local replacement model of their 18-layer language model, built from a 10-million-feature cross-layer transcoder, responded to small perturbations much as the model did one layer after the intervention and increasingly differently over later layers, more in the size of the effect than its direction and slightly more for larger dictionaries, and over 20 prompts the graph's influence of one feature on another ranked the effect of ablating the first on the second with a Spearman correlation of 0.72 | Ameisen et al. (2025), [LIT-1552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1552.md), read in [NOTE-1185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1185.md). It is the method's own measurement of where a circuit read off its stand-in stops being the model's: close for a layer, diverging with depth. It does not say how faithful the circuits of any case study are, which were chosen and validated separately, and it is measured on 18L, not on Claude 3.5 Haiku, where the companion's case studies were run. | Active |
| [THEORY-995](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-995.md) | The attention heads in GPT-2 small that take over the indirect-object prediction when its main name mover heads are knocked out exist because the model was trained with dropout, which optimized it to be robust to disabled components, as Wang, Variengien, Conmy, Shlegeris and Steinhardt hypothesize | Wang et al. (2022), [LIT-1540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1540.md), read in [NOTE-1167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1167.md), §3.4: "We hypothesize that this compensation phenomenon is caused by the use of dropout during training. Thus, the model was optimized for robustness to dysfunctional parts." The compensation is real (a 5% loss of logit difference after knocking out the three name movers); the cause is not examined. Appendix F: "Both the reason and the mechanism of this compensation effect are still unclear." | Proposed |
| [THEORY-996](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-996.md) v2 | On Pythia language models from 410M to 12B parameters, in three single prompt pairs and two small prompt distributions, verifying attention or neuron nodes by activation patching in the order given by attribution patching, a first-order gradient estimate of each node's noising effect, found the nodes with the largest effects at about 2 to 50 times the cost of an oracle ordering, below unordered patching, subsampling and block search in every setting; its misses were concentrated in queries and keys behind saturated attention and in nodes whose direct and indirect effects nearly cancel | Kramár, Lieberum, Shah & Nanda (2024), [LIT-1531](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1531.md), read in [NOTE-1190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1190.md). Ground truth is each node's exact single-node noising effect on the clean prompt's negative log probability. Recomputing the softmax for queries and keys removes many misses; dropping one layer's gradient at a time helps on single prompt pairs but not on the distributions, where AtP with the softmax fix or plain AtP is cheapest. It says nothing about coarser nodes, other model families, effect magnitudes or false positives. | Active |
| [THEORY-998](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-998.md) v2 | In GPT-2 XL, for 1000 facts the model knows, restoring single clean hidden states into a run whose subject tokens were noised recovers the most of the correct object's probability at two sites, middle layers at the last subject token, where MLP outputs carry most of the effect, and late layers at the last token, where attention does; and a rank-one edit of one middle MLP output matrix keyed on the last subject token inserts counterfactual facts that generalize to paraphrases and spare neighbouring subjects better than the fine-tuning, knowledge-neuron and hypernetwork editors tested, working best at that token and in middle layers | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1536.md), read in [NOTE-1166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1166.md): §§2–3, Tables 1 and 4, and Appendices A, B and E. Causal traces: ATE 18.6%; the mid-layer MLP effect at the last subject token peaks at AIE 6.6% against 1.6% for attention. CounterFact on GPT-2 XL: ROME's score 89.2 (efficacy 100.0, paraphrase 96.4, neighbourhood 75.4), next best 66.9. It does not say where facts are stored: a rank-one edit with the same output exists for any one-dimensional fact patch ([LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1000](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1000.md) v2 | For fine-grained nodes of transformer language models generally, attribution patching corrected for attention saturation is a reliable prefilter for activation patching: nodes it ranks low rarely have large single-node patching effects, so verifying nodes in its order finds the important ones at a small multiple of the cost of an oracle, as Kramár et al. expect | Kramár, Lieberum, Shah & Nanda (2024), [LIT-1531](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1531.md), read in [NOTE-1190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1190.md). The measured case is four Pythia models, three prompt pairs and two small distributions. The paper's own diagnostic is what would let a single new setting be checked without exhaustive patching. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1002.md) | On frozen randomly initialized feed-forward networks at chance on hierarchical equality, with 16 input dimensions, distributed alignment search for the two-equality causal model reached interchange intervention accuracy of 0.50 to 0.51 at hidden sizes up to 256 but 0.55 at 1,028 and 0.64 at 4,096, so in a hidden layer much wider than the input a learned rotation can produce above-chance interchange accuracy for an algorithm the network does not implement | Geiger, Wu, Potts, Icard & Goodman (2024), [LIT-1551](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1551.md), §4.4, read in [NOTE-1192](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1192.md). A random network cannot implement hierarchical equality, so any IIA above 0.5 is made by the search. At widths near the input's there is none; at 4,096 there are 14 points. It does not say DAS results on trained networks are artefacts: the trained equality network reached 1.00 at width 16, where the random one stayed at 0.50. | Active |
| [THEORY-1007](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1007.md) | On four subject–verb agreement tasks in Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B, circuits of sparse-autoencoder features and autoencoder error nodes, selected by linear estimates of indirect effect, carried half or more of the behaviour on held-out pairs with about 100 and 500 nodes, where circuits of neurons needed about 1,500 and more than 30,000; with the error nodes removed, the same feature circuits carried little of it, under about a quarter in Pythia and almost none in Gemma | Marks et al. (2025), [LIT-1532](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1532.md), read in [NOTE-1187](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1187.md): §§2–3.2, Figure 3 and Appendices A, B and H. Faithfulness is (m(C) − m(∅))/(m(M) − m(∅)) with nodes outside the circuit mean-ablated, scored on the latter two thirds of each circuit only. The features plus the dense error terms are a small circuit; the features by themselves are not. It says nothing about what the error terms hold, and it does not compare features with neurons on equal terms, which the authors say cannot be done. | Active |
| [THEORY-1011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1011.md) v3 | In autoregressive transformer language models, factual associations are stored in middle-layer MLP modules as linear key–value memories: the MLP takes a key encoding the subject at its last token and returns a value encoding its attributes, which late attention moves to the prediction, and any middle layer could store a given fact equally, as Meng, Bau, Andonian and Belinkov propose | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1536.md), read in [NOTE-1166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1166.md), §2.3 and §3: "the localized factual association hypothesis". It localizes recall along three dimensions, "(i) in the MLP modules (ii) at specific middle layers (iii) and specifically at the processing of the subject's last token", and conjectures "that any fact could be equivalently stored in any one of the middle MLP layers". The support is causal tracing and the success of rank-one edits at the traced site. | Rejected — Hase et al. (LIT-1578, THEORY-1024) meet this entry's own refutation clause for its localization part, in GPT-J on 652 CounterFact facts. ROME rewrites a fact at over 96% at every layer but the last, and the per-fact tracing effect adds at most 3.2 points of R² to edit success. The conjecture that any middle layer could store a fact equally was split out to THEORY-1039 and stays Proposed |
| [THEORY-1014](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1014.md) | In a language model, a behaviour that looks like one mechanism, whether picked out by one contrast or by one cluster of next-token predictions, is often carried by several distinct pathways of sparse features that converge on the output without fully intersecting, as in Pythia-70M's agreement across a relative clause, its prediction of "to" before an infinitival object, and its incrementing of sequences | Marks et al. (2025), [LIT-1532](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1532.md), read in [NOTE-1187](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1187.md): §3.3, §5 and Appendix C. Agreement across a relative clause: subject-number features promote verb forms directly, and a second pathway carries the number to the clause's end through PP/RC boundary features. Cluster 475: one mechanism detects verbs and adjectives that take infinitival objects, another nominal objects before an object complement. Cluster 382: general succession features and token-specific induction features. "While the clusters … seem at first to each represent a single mechanism, circuit-level analysis reveals in both cases a union of distinct mechanisms." | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1020.md) | In a two-layer attention-only language model, on tokens where induction helps, the standard induction circuit (queries and values from the token embedding, keys from the previous-token head) accounts for 35% of the loss its two induction heads contribute, and a hypothesis that adds three-token matching, layer 0's average effect and three layer-0 heads acting as if they attended to the current token accounts for 86% | Chan, Garriga-Alonso, Goldowsky-Dill, Greenblatt, Lin et al. (2022), [LIT-1579](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1579.md), read in [NOTE-1196](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1196.md). Percentages are of 0.053 nats, the loss the induction heads 1.5 and 1.6 contribute on next-token examples whose last token is on an induction-favouring whitelist, measured by causal scrubbing. The naive story's shortfall is mostly in the queries (51% alone) and keys (79%), not the values (90%). It does not say what fraction of the model's whole loss, or of its in-context learning, the circuit explains, nor anything about models with MLPs. | Active |
| [THEORY-1021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1021.md) | In transformer language models, attribution patching agrees well with activation patching for small patches of single heads and their queries, keys, values and attention patterns, for nodes late in a circuit relative to the metric, and for circuits that route information through attention, and agrees badly for large patches such as whole residual streams, for the first MLP layer and the early layers of deep circuits, where nonlinearities move out of saturation, and where an effect needs several features at once, as Nanda proposes | Nanda (2023), [LIT-1581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1581.md), read in [NOTE-1201](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1201.md). The post's map of where the first-order estimate can be trusted. The record holds it from one task in the post, from the mathematics of the estimate ([THEORY-1023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1023.md)), and in part from Kramár et al.'s test on Pythia ([THEORY-996](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-996.md)), which found misses behind saturated attention, as this predicts, and tested no residual-stream nodes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1023.md) | Attribution patching estimates the effect of patching an activation from a clean run into a corrupted run as the difference between the two activations dotted with the gradient of the metric on the corrupted run, so the estimates for every activation come from two forward passes and one backward pass and add over sub-components; the estimate is exact when the metric is affine in the activation, gives no effect for a nonlinearity in saturation whatever the true change, and through LayerNorm ignores the component of a patch along the vector being normalized | Nanda (2023), [LIT-1581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1581.md), read in [NOTE-1201](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1201.md): the estimate and its mathematical properties, not its accuracy in any model. The cost is fixed (about four forward passes for all patches), the estimate is linear and so additive, and its blind spots follow from linearity: saturation, interaction between features, and LayerNorm's scale invariance. | Active |
| [THEORY-1024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1024.md) | In GPT-J, for 652 CounterFact facts the model knows, the per-fact causal-tracing effect at an MLP layer adds at most 3.2 points of explained variance in the success of editing that fact at that layer, beyond what the choice of layer alone explains, across ROME, MEMIT and constrained fine-tuning and five editing objectives; ROME rewrites the fact at over 96% at every layer but the last, including layers where tracing does not place it, and the only reliable link appears when the edit is made on the noised input that tracing uses | Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md): §§4–5, Tables 1–8 and Appendices A–C. For ROME at GPT-J's layer 6, ρ = −0.13 between rewrite score and tracing effect; R² 0.947 from the layer, 0.948 with tracing added. Over twenty method–objective pairs the largest gain is 0.032 (fine-tuning on five layers, Fact Forcing). It does not say that facts are stored nowhere in particular, nor that the layer does not matter: the layer explains most of the variance, and ROME is best on average at the layer tracing favours on average. | Active |
| [THEORY-1025](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1025.md) | The inputs causal scrubbing samples for a treeified hypothesis are the unique maximum-entropy distribution, on finite inputs, among those that give the inputs of every interpretation node the joint distribution they have on the data, so whatever the hypothesis does not claim is resampled as independently as the claims allow | Chan, Garriga-Alonso, Goldowsky-Dill, Greenblatt et al. (2022), [LIT-1583](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1583.md), read in [NOTE-1202](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1202.md), §5. Every node's datum is distributed as D, so each node's scrubbed inputs are jointly as on the data, and among all distributions with that property the algorithm's has the greatest entropy. It characterizes the sampling, not the score: it does not say that a hypothesis whose score matches the model is true, and the same appendix's §7 builds one that is false. | Active |
| [THEORY-1026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1026.md) | In transformer language models, locating where a forward pass carries information about a fact and finding where a weight edit best changes the expressed fact are different questions, because an edit at one layer can override information accumulated across other layers, so that many layers could hold a fact and some happen to, as Hase, Bansal, Kim and Ghandeharioun propose | Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md), §6: "Causal Tracing answers a question about where factual information is carried in representations in a Transformer forward pass, and this question turns out to be a different question than the editing question of where is best to intervene"; and, for why edits work where facts are not traced, "Many layers could store a fact, and it happens that some do". The authors note that this would be surprising, since layers cannot be swapped freely. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1029](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1029.md) | On a three-layer parenthesis-balance classifier, causal-scrubbing hypotheses that resample the terms of one head's input separately scored 81% and 84% of the loss recovered against 77% for the less specific hypothesis they refine, and the authors attribute the rise to resampling washing out a signal, not to a better explanation | Chan, Garriga-Alonso, Goldowsky-Dill, Greenblatt, Lin et al. (2022), [LIT-1580](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1580.md), read in [NOTE-1195](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1195.md). Hypothesis 3a resamples head 2.1's input separately at each of up to 40 positions and recovers 77% (loss 0.97 ± 0.06). Hypotheses 3c and 3d also split each position's input into terms drawn from different inputs, and recover 84% (0.69 ± 0.05) and 81% (0.81 ± 0.05). The authors call the two results not legitimate. It does not say how often this happens in other models, nor that the adversary they propose would remove it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1031.md) | In GPT-J, inserting 10,000 CounterFact counterfactuals at once by a closed-form least-squares update of the MLP output matrices of layers 3 to 8, spread so that each layer writes a share of each fact's required change to the subject's hidden state, gives an editing score of 85.8 (efficacy 98.9, paraphrase 88.6, neighbourhood 73.7) with fluency kept, against 67.6 for weight-decayed fine-tuning, which breaks generation, 50.3 for ROME applied one fact at a time and 23.1 for MEND; GPT-NeoX scores 82.0, and editing late MLPs or attention instead does worse | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1582.md), read in [NOTE-1197](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1197.md): §§4–5, Tables 1 and 2, Appendices A, B and F. On 10,000 true zsRE facts in GPT-J, MEMIT scores 50.7 against FT-W 42.1, MEND 20.0 and ROME 2.6. At a handful of edits ROME generalizes a little better. It does not show where facts are stored: the layer range is chosen from traces averaged over facts, which do not predict per fact where an edit works ([THEORY-1024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1024.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1039](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1039.md) | In autoregressive transformer language models, factual associations are recalled through middle-layer MLP modules acting as key–value memories, and any fact could be stored equally in any one of the middle MLP layers, as Meng, Bau, Andonian and Belinkov conjecture | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1536.md), read in [NOTE-1166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1166.md), §2.3: "we conjecture that any fact could be equivalently stored in any one of the middle MLP layers". It was one clause of [THEORY-1011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1011.md), which is Rejected for its other part, the claim that the traced middle layers are where a fact is stored. Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md), measure edits succeeding at nearly every layer of GPT-J whatever tracing says ([THEORY-1024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1024.md)). That is what this conjecture predicts, but it is not evidence of storage, since an edit can work wherever a layer can write the needed output ([LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1061](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1061.md) | Flack makes downward causation operational as components tuning their behaviour to their own estimates of aggregate variables they collectively compute: weak (apparent) when at least one component tunes to a variable slower than the behaviour producing it, strong (effective) when the variable is predictive, robust, used nearly universally, agreed on and gaining mutual information with the microscopic behaviour; she speaks of a new level only at the strong form, and regeneration of the variable by its use is not among her criteria | Flack (2017), [LIT-1630](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1630.md), read in [NOTE-1216](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1216.md), §1, §3 and §7. Active as a reading of what the paper proposes, which its text states as lists. It does not say the proposal is right, that it meets any definition of causation (the paper sets that aside), or that the macaque system meets the strong criteria; the evidence for that is in earlier papers not reproduced here. The sharp edge for the record: what reinforces itself in Flack is the convergence of members' estimates, not the variable's persistence. | Active |
